en.title: Weekly Global Macro — Energy is returning to the market, but financing the next wave of investment is becoming harder
en.deck: The IEA's structural energy outlook and the ECB's financial stability assessment expose a shared constraint: restoring physical resilience requires capital just as technology financing faces a reassessment of expected returns. An evidence-led study of the week of 16–22 November.
en.regime: Partial recovery of physical energy supply, persistent delivery constraints and selective financing pressure.
en.key_risk: A feedback loop between delayed infrastructure investment, recurring delivered-energy costs and tighter financing; conditional, not a measured systemic crisis.
watch: Onshore oil stocks and refined-product exports
Hyperscaler issuance and operating cash flows

signal_rationale.delta: The 19 November IEA WEO introduces a structural capital-allocation and dependency perspective to the 18 November ECB financial-stability diagnosis; unlike the 21 November daily market report, this assessment tests the link between physical energy availability and the ability to finance the next wave of productive investment.
signal_rationale.evidence: IEA November oil supply 105.4 mb/d, observed stocks +52 mb, oil on water +86 mb, OECD stocks -47 mb; WEO scenarios and Asian exposure; ECB FSR boxes 3 and 4 on hyperscaler cash flow and >USD 200bn USD IG issuance; Friday cross-asset closing data; China fixed investment and producer/consumer prices; US G17 capacity utilization; Eurostat inflation contributions; Bank Indonesia and SARB decisions; APEC declaration.
signal_rationale.scale_path: Fuel delivery, inventory location and refining affect input costs and real income; substitution shifts demand toward grids and mineral processing; technology funding concentration and exchange-rate constraints affect project financing and subsequent productive capacity.
signal_rationale.transmission: Conditional physical energy constraints → delivered costs → inflation and financing constraints → investment delays; AI repricing and external debt exposures can amplify financing pressures or release capacity if demand falls. Distinguish stocks, flows, market valuations, policy actions and scenario outputs.
signal_rationale.falsifier: Simultaneous recovery in land-based inventories, refined product supply, credit issuance conditions and operating cash flow would weaken both proposed adverse feedback channels; independent demand and physical capacity evidence can distinguish alternative explanations.

key_constraints: Week 16–22 November; information cutoff 22 November 23:59 BRT; retrospective revision made 27 November, not contemporaneous publication.
IEA OMR observed inventories include overlapping totals and components; supply, throughput and product flows are not interchangeable.
IEA WEO conditional scenario projections are not realized observations or committed projects; modeled copper gap is scenario-specific.
ECB hyperscaler capital-expenditure projection is an external estimate; issuance, cash flow and market valuation are distinct; euro-area bank NPL ratio uses significant institutions in Q2 2026.
Market reporting uses dated session windows and distinguishes daily and weekly changes; no complete global synchronized closing dataset or portfolio flow estimates.
China industrial value added covers enterprises above designated size; nominal export values are not volume; investment categories can overlap.
US G17 uses 17 November release vintage, before scheduled annual revision.
APEC voluntary declaration is not enacted tariff or measured trade impact.
Selective regional evidence, not exhaustive world survey; QA and full CI/deployment pending.
